verdicts.claim: L1 sub-claim: lean_failed is unreachable for K>=2 because every count_block_at failure is already a phase-0 visit_block_at failure on the same block, and that failure is handled before phase A
verdicts.evidence: count_block_at (full_ball_tower.hpp:2843-2863) can fail in only four ways: require regular_rank (2851), extra.at (2858; `extra` is a std::unordered_map at 1690, so it throws std::out_of_range), table.rank(k) (2859), and require absent_scheduled_block (2860). visit_block_at (2866-2907) makes the same calls in the same branches (2873, 2888-2890), and only then runs its own extra cardinality requires. Phase 0 visits every position of programs[current_k] (2560-2584), with current_k = K (1028) and orders[k-1].k = k (790). parallel_items rethrows any exception it captured (pool.hpp:370-382, 420-441), so prepare_static_order throws for K. Overlapped path: ready[K-1] is set only when phase 0 built (1036-1039); otherwise runner K returns without calling order_lots (949-955), and static_failure is thrown before any phase-A failure (1064). Non-overlapped path (run_orders_parallel): phase 0 of every K runs outside any try, before any order_lots (792-800). order_lots is called only from these two paths (819, 975); the batch-resolver and single-thread paths use prepare_block (631, 641, 667).

verdicts.claim: L1: taking c, m, iota and the regular/extra flag from phase 0's collection loop and dropping order_prepare_lean for K>=2 leaves the published object unchanged
verdicts.evidence: On non-mutant code the count equals the number of emits: n_shell emits (2877-2885) against return n_shell (2855); strict_components.size() emits (2893) against the same size (2862). The contribution and interior come from the same visit call (2564-2565, 2869-2871 and 2891, compared with 2847-2848 and 2861). The facet-to-target association is unchanged, because ordinals are program position then visit order (2585-2621). tower_work does not contain helper_threads: it is tower_detail, 'never tower_work' (87-95; tower_probe.cpp:425-431). same_work and static_counters exclude thread metadata (full_ball_tower_gate.cpp:345-347; task_pool_gate.cpp:537-539).
verdicts.conditions: (i) c_j must be the count of phase-0 emits for position j (or count_block_at), and m and iota must come from the same visit. (ii) The lean arrays must be delivered by the same swap as static_targets (1032, 797), so a failed phase 0 never hands over partial data. (iii) anchor_blocks, regular_blocks and extra_blocks must still be incremented per block, before the failure checks (1243-1244), using a per-position flag. A per-order sum changes the tower counters published on a failed build (see L10). (iv) K1 has no phase 0 (1026: k >= 2), so it keeps order_prepare_lean. (v) After L1, the COUNT_SKIPS_FACET mutant (2852-2853) acts only on K1, through lean_k1 and the k1_facets_unconsumed check (1393). Its kill (CMakeLists.txt:862-870) then depends on K1 regular facet blocks; retarget it as proposed.

verdicts.claim: L2: no catalogue access in the sequential loop ((a) prefetch of balls[program[j+16]]; (b) store a u32 BallId per batch and materialise ExactLevel later) leaves the object unchanged
verdicts.evidence: The batch level is copied from balls[program[begin]].level (1378, then 1297/1342). The encoder gives every node and contribution its batch level (full_coverage_certificate.hpp:365-386). ExactLevel is unreduced ('non reduit', lanes/level.hpp:36-38; operator== compares the representation at 39-41), and tower_digest hashes num and den of node and contribution levels (tower_chain.cpp:1121-1126, 1176, 1187). Two balls of the same lot have equal level_run, so equal exact values (1962-1966), but not necessarily the same representation. The only reader of flat.level is the encoder's FlatDraftSource (certificate.hpp:211-212); batches() is d.level.size().
verdicts.conditions: (b) must store exactly program[begin], the first program position of the lot. Any other ball of the lot, for example the first published group's ball, can change the digest. The K1 zero batch (1358, 1364) needs a sentinel. Levels must be materialised before encoding (finish, 724-732), and the encoder checks (coverage_nonincreasing_batch, coverage_positive_level_required, coverage_invalid_level) must still run on the materialised values. (a) The prefetch index must be bounds-checked, as at 1257-1265, because forming &x[i] beyond the end is UB even without a load. The regular/extra part inherits L1's condition (iii).

verdicts.claim: L3: dense program positions (pos_of per order, anchors indexed by position, 'anchored and strictly lower' <=> pos < lot_begin, slow path re-deriving the reason) preserve the object, IDs, failure statuses and their order
verdicts.evidence: programs[k] are subsequences of by_level (2026-2035), so each ball occurs at most once per order. level_run is non-decreasing along by_level (1993-1999), and lots are maximal equal-run intervals (1376-1380). Anchors are written only for program balls and only after their lot closes (1301, 1350). So for t in the program: pos(t) < lot_begin <=> (level_run[t] < run and anchors[t] != absent). For t outside the program or t >= |balls|, today's reason is not_strict if (t >= |balls| or level_run[t] >= run), else closed_anchor_missing (1267-1268). A scratch toy compared the first (position, facet, reason) of both formulations on 20,000 random programs with out-of-range, non-program, same-lot, later-lot and valid targets: all equal (19,619 failing, 381 fully valid). Toy file: scratchpad/phaseA/verify_object_safety/toy_checks.py, SHA-256 0c9159da…
verdicts.conditions: (i) Phase 0 must never refuse a target that is outside the program. It must emit a sentinel and keep the BallId, or its level_run, so the reason is re-derived at the consuming facet in phase A. A phase-0 refusal would be reported first (1064, ahead of 1095-1099) and would suppress that order's phase-A counters, which changes the published reason and tower_work. (ii) t >= |balls| maps to not_strict. (iii) Phase C of K+1 reads lower->anchors[birth_ball] (1575-1577). That needs pos_of_K kept alive until phase C of K+1, a pos_of_1 for K1 (which has no phase 0), and the vertical_birth_anchor reason re-derived for balls outside the program. (iv) anchor_duplicate (1300, 1349) becomes tautological. (v) static_grouping_gate compares traces between the hashed and sorted paths (static_grouping_gate.cpp:153-159, 235); both must translate the same way.

verdicts.claim: L3 side claim (spec section 10): position indexing cuts resident anchors at K10 from about 10 x 22 MB to about 10 x 8 MB
verdicts.evidence: Phase C of K+1 still needs BallId -> position of order K for births (1575-1577). pos_of_K is 4*|balls| per order and lives from phase 0 of K until phase C of K+1, the same size and lifetime as today's anchors (760, 1355). The cut holds only if the birth lookup is re-expressed, for example as a per-order bitmap plus popcount rank over by_level.
verdicts.conditions: Holds only if the birth-anchor lookup no longer needs an O(|balls|) u32 map per order.

verdicts.claim: L4: u32 node tokens inside phase A (compressed, next, roots, owners, parent CSR and offsets), widened at the encoder, leave the object unchanged
verdicts.evidence: order_new_node refuses id >= kAbsent32 (1165), so every node ID fits in u32 with kAbsent32 as a sentinel, and sort, unique and comparisons are unchanged. No bound limits the parents or contributions per order: facets are unbounded outside the hashed path (2602-2603), and blocks are at most BallId max. MonotoneHistoryOf tests `next == absent` against the u64 sentinel (410-416). K1 images are the u64 `absent` (1571, 1584), and lower_nodes are hashed as u64 (tower_chain.cpp:1196-1197; FullNodeId = u64, full_certificate.hpp:19).
verdicts.conditions: (i) Keep batch_begin, parent_begin and contribution_begin as u64/size_t. u32 offsets need a new refusal, which is a changed status beyond 2^32-1 entries per order. (ii) A templated MonotoneHistoryOf must compare next against the token type's own sentinel; otherwise every node looks linked and fails lower_history_edge. (iii) image and lower_nodes stay u64 with the u64 absent. A kAbsent32 that is zero-extended changes K1's lower_nodes and the digest. (iv) The public FullCoverageFlatDraft stays u64, via a widened copy or a templated source.

verdicts.claim: L5: allocation-free grouped lots (per-runner scratch, u32 dsu/owners, groups as a CSR by counting sort on the min representative) preserve IDs, contribution order, counters and failure order
verdicts.evidence: The union writes dsu[max(a,b)] = min(a,b) on roots (1313), so each component's root is its smallest block index. Groups are enumerated as groups[find(b)] for ascending b, then by root index (1315-1319), which gives group order by min position with blocks ascending inside each group. A stable counting sort on the min label reproduces this; a scratch toy checked 20,000 random lots, with a different connected-components algorithm, and found identical group lists. Parent order is normalised by sort and unique (1330-1331).
verdicts.conditions: Keep the per-group loop order for contributions (1325-1328), distinct_births (1336), node creation and its u32 refusal (1337, 1165), inert_blocks (1346), grouped_lots and lot_dsu_slots before the loop (1304-1305), and anchors written after all groups (1348-1351). Where a bad_alloc occurs will change; that depends on resources and is not part of the deterministic object.

verdicts.claim: L6-L7: first touch, THP (madvise), workspace reuse and extra prefetching do not change the object
verdicts.evidence: Prefetches and madvise have no effect on values. Existing prefetches are bounds-checked (1257-1265, 1387). Anchors of a lot are written only after it closes (1301, 1350), so an anchor value read ahead of consumption can be absent or stale. RSS is published as peak_rss_kb (tower_probe.cpp:417-418); it is not tower_work and not the digest.
verdicts.conditions: (i) Every prefetch index must be bounds-checked. (ii) The 'two-stage pipeline' replacing the demand load at 1263 may use the value read ahead only as a prefetch address; the anchor that is consumed must be re-read at 1268-1269. (iii) Pre-touching must not write into std::vector capacity beyond size(), which is UB; use sized RawVector or an allocator. (iv) Workspaces reused across frames must be fully reset: anchors to absent, o.st to zero, cursors, lot_blocks. Otherwise anchor_duplicate or tower_work doubling follows.

verdicts.claim: L8: no nested pool / a global thread budget for runner and helper work does not change the object
verdicts.evidence: The helpers write by index. order_prepare_lean selects the first failing chunk by index (1190-1206), independent of the executor. Phase-B rows go to fixed slots (1531-1539). Runner-created threads are counted in helper_threads through spawned_threads (pool.hpp:355; full_ball_tower.hpp:594-597), which is tower_detail, excluded from tower_work and same_work (full_ball_tower_gate.cpp:345-347). A failed thread launch today gives the resource status full_ball_thread_launch_failed (3058-3059).
verdicts.conditions: A pool with several submitters must keep per-index outputs and failure selection by minimum index. parallel_items' 'first captured' exception (pool.hpp:370-382) is nondeterministic, so it is acceptable only where exceptions are resource-only. The thread-launch refusal and the --unwind gate scenarios (CMakeLists.txt:246-247) change coverage; that depends on resources, not on the object. helper_threads, pool_jobs and static_lanes_used will change.

verdicts.claim: L9: a K1 site -> domain-index table replaces visit + point_id + lower_bound per facet and lean_k1 without changing the object
verdicts.evidence: The domain is the sorted point_id of every site in [0, |upos|), with duplicates refused (1784-1790). So rank_of[identity[r].second] = r equals lower_bound(domain, point_id(s)) (1216) for every valid site. A facet's site still comes from the ball record inside visit_block_at (shell_ids at 2880-2884, census ids via geometry_id, which does its own lookup and unknown_identity require at 2046-2049), so 'replaces visit' is inaccurate. Only point_id + lower_bound can be removed.
verdicts.conditions: Keep enumerating facets in visit order, the facet.size()==1 check (1214), and the bound min(n, lean_failed) (1211). If the K1 loop is parallelised, the reported failure must be the one at the smallest position; today it is sequential.

verdicts.claim: L10: batching the counters (representatives = sum c, anchor_blocks = M, lot counters from lot sizes, one checked add per order) is risk-free for tower_work
verdicts.evidence: After a success the sums are equal, and same_work compares all of these counters (full_ball_tower_gate.cpp:333-349). tower_work is also published when a build fails: tower_chain.cpp:1962 sets tower_stats before the status check; the probe prints tower_work unconditionally (tower_probe.cpp:385-398) and then returns 3 (442); order counters are merged on every exception (1122-1124, 842-843). Today anchor_blocks, regular and extra are added before the lean_failed throw (1243-1245), and representatives per facet before each guard (1248-1268). A mid-order failure therefore publishes the prefix, as the witness does (prepare_block 2910-2916). Toy case: failure at block 3, facet 1, with c = [2,1,0,3,2]: per-facet adds give 5, a batched sum gives 8, and adding at the end gives 0. No existing gate would notice. The failure gate checks only floors (order_failure_priority_gate.cpp:107, 293), and its phase-A failpoint fires after the loop (1405), when the counters are complete.
verdicts.conditions: When a failure is thrown, the batched version must add the exact prefix: sum of c_i for i < j plus (f+1) for representatives; j+1 blocks for anchor_blocks, regular and extra; singleton, grouped and lot_dsu_slots only for lots that reached order_lot, including grouped_lots and lot_dsu_slots already added at 1304-1305 before a distinct_births failure in the same lot. The alternative is to declare the change in tower_work after a failure and add a gate for it.

verdicts.claim: L11: RawVector for fully overwritten arrays (lean arrays 1183-1185) and a parallel anchors fill are risk-free
verdicts.evidence: A chunk stops at its first failing block (1199-1201), leaving the rest of its range unwritten. reserve_lean then sums every lean_count entry (1227). With RawVector that is an indeterminate read (UB). A garbage sum can turn the lean failure into full_ball_size_overflow or full_ball_allocation_failed at reserve (1234, 3052-3055), before the loop reaches lean_failed (1245). Today the zero fill makes the sum harmless.
verdicts.conditions: reserve_lean must sum only [0, lean_failed), or the failing chunk must zero the rest of its range. The parallel anchors fill must finish before the loop and before phase C reads anchors (1576). With L1, phase 0 writes every K>=2 position whenever it succeeds, so only K1 is exposed.

verdicts.claim: L12: fusing the live count (live = n0 + births + merges - sum|parents|) is risk-free, and keeping the check preserves final_component_count
verdicts.evidence: Every parent passes next==absent in order_root (1156) before any node of its lot is created. Groups of a lot have disjoint roots by construction (1311-1319), and parents are deduplicated (1273-1274, 1330-1331). So the scan (1402-1404) equals births + merges - sum of |parents| over node-creating actions. Scratch toy, 4,000 instances of the spec transliteration: equal. The literal formula counts the K1 domain twice, because births already includes the domain nodes (1369 -> 1170). It is off by n on all 2,000 K1 toy instances and would fail every K1 build loudly. The encoder never checks a final live count (certificate.hpp:320-388). The top order's `next` is read by nobody else: successors are recomputed by the encoder, and phase C reads only lower orders' next (1560-1561).
verdicts.conditions: Use births + merges - sum of |parents| over merges only, or |next| - that sum. Do not add n0. Exclude continuation parents: flat.parent.size() includes published continuations. Keep the check after 1393 and 1398. The fused guard no longer checks `next` independently: a faulty next write, silent for the top order, would be caught by the scan and missed by the fused count.

verdicts.claim: L13: a flat per-lot u32 root buffer instead of std::vector<u64> per Block leaves the object unchanged
verdicts.evidence: The singleton path tests roots.size()==1 (1290) and passes the roots as parents (1293, 1298). The encoder refuses unsorted or duplicate parents (certificate.hpp:329-332).
verdicts.conditions: Keep the per-block sort and unique (1273-1274) before order_lot. Reset the offsets per lot. u32 values inherit L4's conditions.

summary:
I checked all thirteen lightening candidates against the code at f44a8db03 (worktree 22eb467cb; full_ball_tower.hpp SHA-256 124d3e9b…). None of them is unconditionally "risk: none". Each keeps the published object (digest, IDs, the failure reported and its priority, tower_work) only under specific conditions. GCP was not used and the repository was not modified. The only thing I ran is an abstract Python toy: `/tmp/claude-1000/-workspaces-E-HGP/71988aca-a49a-4d33-96db-f05468331005/scratchpad/phaseA/verify_object_safety/toy_checks.py` (SHA-256 0c9159da…, output in `toy_checks.txt` beside it). It found L3 (20,000 random programs), L5 (20,000 random lots) and L12 (4,000 instances) consistent with the code, and it prints the L10 failure example.

**L1's central claim holds.** Every way `count_block_at` can fail, `visit_block_at` fails the same way on the same block. Phase 0 visits every position of the order's program. A phase-0 failure keeps phase A of that order from running on both static paths, and it is reported first. So `lean_failed` cannot be reached for K≥2.

**Traps found in the other candidates:**
1. **Failure-path counters (L10, and L1 if it sums the regular/extra flags).** tower_work is published even when the build fails (`tower_chain.cpp:1962`, `tower_probe.cpp:385`). Today the counters are added per block and per facet before each check, so a failed build publishes the work done up to the failure. Batched sums publish a different number (toy: 5 today, against 8 or 0). No existing gate would catch this.
2. **Batch level (L2b).** The stored ball must be exactly `program[begin]`, the lot's first program position. ExactLevel is not reduced, and the digest hashes its num/den.
3. **Position indexing (L3).**
   - Phase 0 must not refuse a target outside the program. It must keep the BallId so phase A re-derives the same reason on the facet that consumes it; otherwise the failure is reported with phase-0 priority.
   - Phase C needs `pos_of` of the order below for births, and K1 needs a `pos_of` built even though it has no phase 0.
   - Because `pos_of` stays resident as long as the anchors do today, the section 10 claim of 10 × 22 MB → 10 × 8 MB at K10 is refuted.
4. **u32 tokens (L4).**
   - The CSR offsets must stay u64; u32 offsets would need a new refusal.
   - The absent sentinel must be translated inside a templated MonotoneHistoryOf.
   - `lower_nodes` must stay u64 with the u64 absent value, or K1's part of the digest changes.
5. **RawVector for the lean arrays (L11).** `reserve_lean` would read slots that are never written after a chunk's first failure. That is undefined behaviour, and it can turn the reported failure into an allocation or size-overflow refusal.
6. **Fused live count (L12).**
   - The formula as written counts the K1 domain twice, because `births` already includes those nodes. Every K1 build would fail loudly.
   - The sum of parents must cover node-creating actions only, not continuations.
   - The fused check no longer tests the `next` array independently, and nothing else reads the top order's `next`.
7. **Prefetch pipeline (L7).** The value read ahead may serve only as a prefetch address. The anchor must be re-read when the facet consumes it.

**Remaining candidates.** L5, L6, L8, L9 and L13 are safe under local conditions:
- L5: keep the group order by smallest position and the per-group loop order.
- L6: bounds-checked addresses, no writes past a vector's size, and a full reset when workspaces are reused across frames.
- L8: failures still chosen by smallest index. Thread counters change, but they are not part of tower_work.
- L9: the table matches `lower_bound` exactly, but the per-facet visit is still needed to know each facet's site.
- L13: keep the per-block sort and unique.
missing: No C++ build, CTest gate or probe was run (the host is saturated and the repository is read-only); every verdict rests on reading the code plus an abstract Python toy, which is not a qualification.
The toy covers only the combinatorics of L3 guard equivalence, L5 group order, L12 live count and one L10 failure example. It does not exercise the engine, the encoder or the digest.
No existing gate compares tower_work exactly after a mid-loop phase-A failure. A gate for that case is needed before L10, or L1 with summed flags, can be qualified.
local_plateau::ShellTable::rank() was assumed to throw the same way on both call sites (count_block_at and visit_block_at make the same call); its body was not read.
Not analysed: liveness, deadlock and TSan behaviour of a multi-submitter pool (L8/P5), and the effect of THP or madvise on G4 (L6).
Not analysed for object safety: the parallelisation hypotheses P0-P5.

verdicts.claim: (1) The invariant on writes to compressed: `compressed[p]` is only ever assigned a node on p's successor chain. This covers every writer: the new node, path compression, the K1 domain nodes and any reset.
verdicts.evidence:
Every writer of OrderState::compressed (full_ball_tower.hpp:762) in the phase-A static path is listed by `grep -n compressed`:
- 1166 `push_back(id)`: a self-loop. The K1 domain nodes come through `order_new_node(o, zero, {}, kAbsent32)` at 1369, with no parents.
- 1167 `compressed[parent]=id`: written in the same statement as `next[parent]=id`, so the value is next(parent).
- 1154 path compression `compressed[token]=r`: r is reached from token by chasing compressed (1152), so by induction and transitivity r is on token's successor chain.
- The only reset is the swap at 1401, after the loop. Lines 640/704/2054-2056/2940-2941 touch the builder's own `compressed` (1693), used by the sequential witness path: a different object.

The induction needs `next` to be write-once, and it is:
- parents always come from `order_root`, which requires `next[r]==absent` (1156);
- roots are deduplicated per block (1273-1274) and per group (1330-1331);
- they are disjoint across groups, because the lot DSU merges any blocks that share a root (1306-1316);
- no node is created between the root reads and the lot's writes (1388-1390).

So successor chains only grow at their tail. `id=next.size()` (1164) is larger than every parent, so chains strictly increase: no cycles, and `compressed[x]==x` iff x is live.

Simulation (`verify_p1/p1_sim.py`, SHA-256 prefix 75f13119…, seeds 1 and 20260926, 2,600 instances): at every write, plain and hinted, the stored value was checked against the successor chain as it stood at that moment. There were 0 violations.

Corollary used below: every value ever stored in `compressed[x]`, stale or fresh, stays on succ*(x) for the rest of the order.

verdicts.claim: (2a) No vector reallocation of compressed/next while a helper reads them.
verdicts.evidence:
`reserve_lean` reserves `nodes = blocks + (k==1 ? domain.size() : 0)` (1228-1229). The loop creates at most one node per block: at most once on the singleton path (1293), and once per non-empty group on the grouped path (1337), with groups ≤ blocks. So N ≤ n0 + M ≤ capacity, and `push_back` cannot reallocate after 1374. The simulation's max nodes/capacity ratio is exactly 1.000, and the toy checks `data()` equality at the end.

However:
- the K1 domain nodes are pushed at 1365-1370, BEFORE `reserve_lean` (1374), and may regrow the vector there;
- `o.anchors` is assigned at 1355.
verdicts.conditions:
- Start the helper only after 1374.
- The helper reads through raw pointers captured after reserve. It must never call `size()` or `operator[]` on the vector object: `push_back` writes `_M_finish` concurrently, which is a data race on the vector itself.
- Better: a fixed-capacity RawVector of n0+M, with a `data()`-equality self-check.
- Stop and join the helper before the frees at 1394-1401 (`lean_*`, `static_targets`, `compressed`) and on every throw from inside the loop (1150, 1156, 1165, 1245, 1250, 1254, 1267, 1268, 1292, 1300, 1336, 1349, 1384).
- `parallel_detail::JoinThreads` (`pool.hpp:84-90`) only joins. A helper waiting on an anchor that is never written would deadlock the join, so a stop flag must be set first.

verdicts.claim: (2b) A hint read concurrently with RELAXED atomics, while the committer path-compresses and appends nodes, is always an ancestor-or-self of the anchor (no torn values, no reads beyond size).
verdicts.evidence:
Torn values are excluded: `atomic_ref<u64>` on an aligned `vector<u64>` element is lock-free on x86-64. But relaxed alone does not give ancestry.

A new node's slot is constructed by a plain `push_back` (1166) before the parent store (1167). If the helper reads `compressed[parent]==id` with a relaxed load, then reads `compressed[id]`:
- with `std::vector` there is no happens-before between the construction and the read. That is a data race on a not-yet-constructed element in [size, capacity): UB;
- with a pre-sized, zero-filled array (all-atomic, so TSan is silent), the helper can read 0, which is NOT on the chain.

The Python model of that case (seed 20260926, 2,000 instances) published 932 non-ancestor hints and corrupted or failed 293 of 2,000 runs. The `< prior_count` test caught none of them, because 0 < prior.

Today's committer writes at 1154, 1167 and 1301/1350 are plain. The C++ toy under TSan (`setarch -R`, `--racy`) reports exactly three data races, at the parent store, the path-compression store and the anchor store, while still producing an identical object. The UB is silent on x86.

verdicts.claim: (3) Accepting a hint iff hint < prior_count of the current lot is necessary and sufficient. Roots must be read at the open cut, so a node created in the current lot must be rejected.
verdicts.evidence:
**Sufficient, given ancestry.** Suppose hint ∈ succ*(anchor) in the final history and hint < prior_count(λ). Every node on the chain from the anchor to the hint is < hint, and each `next` link was written when its target was created, so the whole chain exists at the open cut. Chasing from the hint (1152) then ends at the same live root as chasing from the anchor. The checks at 1150/1156 see the same r.
- Python, adversarial hints drawn anywhere on the anchor's FINAL chain (stale, fresh or 'future', as a load-buffering execution could deliver): 2,000 of 2,000 instances byte-identical on `next`, `birth_ball`, `runs`, anchors, the flat draft, nine counters and live count. 61,237 hints ≥ prior were rejected and 68,242 used.
- Adding the cheap check anchor ≤ hint < prior: also 2,000 of 2,000.

**Necessity is narrower than stated.** During `order_block_lean` of lot λ, `next.size()==prior_count` (1383, 1388-1390): no node of λ exists before `order_lot` (1390). So in every sequentially consistent (SC) execution a consumed hint is automatically < prior. Hints ≥ prior never occurred in:
- 95,360 used hints of the interleaved Python model;
- 24,230 hints accepted by the -O2 C++ toy;
- 1,362 hints accepted under TSan.

The test is required only (a) if hint slots are relaxed, where the C++ model allows load buffering, and (b) against design errors. With a release store of each hint and an acquire load, load buffering is excluded and the test becomes a defence. Without the test, a hint ≥ prior reaches the require at 1150 and throws a spurious `full_ball_anchor_not_prior`, or reads unconstructed memory if that require is bypassed. It is never a silent wrong object: the noprior mutant gave 1,794 of 2,000 out-of-bounds failures and 0 silent mismatches.

verdicts.claim: (4) Counters: P1 changes counters in tower_work (e.g. find steps / path writes), which may matter for the digest or for gates comparing tower_work.
verdicts.evidence:
The worry is unfounded, so the neutrality claim holds.
- Phase A's `order_root` counts nothing (1149-1158). Phase A's `add()` calls touch only object quantities, unchanged by hints: 1243-1244, 1248, 1170, 1285, 1288, 1299, 1304-1305, 1327, 1346.
- `lower_find_steps` and `lower_path_writes` belong to phase C (`MonotoneHistoryOf::find/unite`, 456-470). They run on its OWN `parent` array, built by iota from `next_of` (399-403), and are independent of phase A's `compressed`.
- `tower_work` (`tower_probe.cpp:386-399`; `task_pool_gate.cpp:527-533`) has no hop counters.
- `same_work` (`full_ball_tower_gate.cpp:330-356`) and `static_counters` (`task_pool_gate.cpp:536-545`) compare only fields that stay deterministic.
- `tower_digest` hashes object data only.

The toy's committer hop count changes (e.g. 14,025,682 → 13,992,717), but that is not a product counter.
verdicts.conditions:
- Any new hint counters (accepted, rejected, missing, commit hops) depend on timing. They must be metadata, never in `tower_work`, `same_work` or `static_counters`, or the paired and thread-count gates become flaky.
- The helper thread changes scheduling metadata. R22 probe_0 shows `runner_threads` 5, `helper_threads` 409, `pool_threads` 47 at K5; P1 adds 5 (K5) or 10 (K10).
- `task_pool_gate.cpp:608` sums the created threads, and its floor `threads_on < threads_off` (647) survives only if both arms get the helper.
- Count the helper in a new field so parallelism stays measured.

verdicts.claim: (5a) The published object (and statuses) are byte-identical to the sequential phase A under P1.
verdicts.evidence:
This follows from (1), (3), the canonical-root argument (the root is the unique live node, so compression changes only cost) and unchanged failure checks.
- Python, interleaved committer + helper under a random scheduler with stale reads: 6,000 of 6,000 runs identical, 0 non-ancestor hints, 0 invariant violations.
- C++ toy at -O2: 400 of 400 identical (M ≤ 20,000, 6.64 M facets).
- C++ toy under TSan: 40 of 40 identical.

On this saturated host (load ~35 on 8 CPUs) the toy's helper hinted only about 0.4 % of facets, so timing coverage is thin. The deterministic adversarial mode is the real coverage of the accept/reject branches.

verdicts.claim: (5b) The two proposed mutants ('hint used as root without chasing', 'hint accepted without the < prior_count test') can be killed by tests that force a large lead or an overtaking helper.
verdicts.evidence:
No lead or lag can produce a consumed hint ≥ prior in an SC execution, because lot λ's nodes are created after its hints are consumed (1383-1390).
- The C++ toy with the no-prior mutant: 400 of 400 runs identical with 0 rejections, so the mutant SURVIVES natural runs.
- Killing it needs a deterministic `MHGP9_TESTING` hook that injects hints, e.g. random nodes of the anchor's final chain taken from a first run. Then the mutant throws `anchor_not_prior` at 1150 (Python: 1,794 of 2,000 failures).
- The no-chase mutant is killed by the same hook with stale hints. The check `next[r]==absent` at 1156 raises `root_not_prior`, or the parents differ (Python: 1,623 failures plus 32 silent mismatches when both requires are bypassed).
- A 'missing acquire / placeholder read' mutant is invisible to TSan when all accesses are atomic, so it needs the injection hook plus review.

verdicts.claim: The commit's per-facet work drops to a sequential hint read plus next[hint].
verdicts.evidence:
For the failure order to stay the same, the committer still reads `level_run[target]` (1267) and `anchors[target]` (1268) at random, then `compressed[hint]` at least twice (1152-1153, plus hops if the hint is stale) and `next[r]` (1156). That leaves at least 4 random touches per facet, although the anchors → compressed dependency is broken.

The helper also reads lines of `compressed` and `anchors` that the committer writes (path compression and parent stores), which adds coherence traffic across cores or CCDs. Prior audits bound the upside:
- `PHASE_A_GRAPHE_TEMPOREL_20260923.md:125-130`: root searches ≤ 32 % of local phase-A cycles at K10;
- the same note, line 183: the physical-head ablation gave no stable gain.

verdicts.claim: Expected effect of P1: ÷1.3–2 on A(K) if chains dominate.
verdicts.evidence: This is a projection. No G4 or local measurement of P1 exists, and none can be made on this saturated host. The prior ablations cited above point against chain dominance.

summary:
Pin: `full_ball_tower.hpp` at f44a8db03 (= 22eb467cb, SHA-256 124d3e9b…). Read-only on the repository; GCP not used.

**Verdict.** P1 is sound in principle but not as stated.
- **Invariant on writes to `compressed`: holds.** The only writers are 1166 (self), 1167 (a new parent, equal to `next[parent]`) and 1154 (a root reached from the token). `next` is write-once, and the only reset is 1401, after the loop. So any value ever stored in `compressed[x]` is an ancestor-or-self of x for the rest of the order.
- **Hint-validity rule: holds with conditions.** Accepting a hint iff hint < prior_count gives byte identity, *given* that the hint really is on the anchor's chain.

**Where the claim is wrong or incomplete.**
1. **"Relaxed atomics" is not enough (2b refuted).**
   - A new node's slot is constructed by a plain `push_back` (1166) before the relaxed parent store (1167). Following that id without an acquire reads a slot whose construction the helper has not synchronised with: UB with `std::vector`.
   - With a pre-sized zero array the helper can read a 0 placeholder, which is not on the chain and passes the prior test. Python: 932 non-ancestor hints, 293 of 2,000 runs corrupted.
   - Fix: either (i) the helper never follows a node ≥ an acquire-loaded committed count, or (ii) the new-id stores at 1167 are release and the helper's loads acquire.
   - Today's plain committer stores at 1154, 1167 and 1301/1350 must become `atomic_ref`. TSan on the toy's racy mode flags exactly these three sites. The protected toy is TSan-clean: 0 warnings, 40 of 40 identical.
2. **Reallocation (2a holds with conditions).** No reallocation can happen after `reserve_lean` (1228-1229, N ≤ n0+M, from 1293/1337). But the K1 domain nodes are pushed before it (1365-1370). The helper must start after 1374, use captured raw pointers (never `size()` or `operator[]`), and be stopped + joined before 1394-1401 and on every throw. `JoinThreads` alone (`pool.hpp:84-90`) could deadlock.
3. **The prior test (3).**
   - It never fires in an SC run: no node of the current lot exists while its facets are resolved (1383-1390). 0 hints ≥ prior among 95,360 (Python), 24,230 (toy -O2) and 1,362 (toy under TSan) used hints.
   - It is needed only against load buffering (if hint slots are relaxed) and design bugs. Without it, 1150 throws a spurious failure; the object is never silently wrong.
   - It does NOT check identity: hints from another facet, garbage < prior, zero placeholders and an untagged ring all corrupt silently. Use one slot per facet ordinal (5.4 MB u32 at K5 order 5, 15.3 MB at K10 order 10) or ordinal-tagged slots, and keep 1267/1268 in the committer.
4. **Counters (4 holds).** `tower_work`, `same_work`, `static_counters` and the digest are unaffected. Phase A counts no hops, and the phase-C find counters (456-470) use their own `parent` array (399-403).
   - Any hint counter must be metadata only.
   - Thread metadata will change (R22 probe_0: 5 runners, 409 helper threads, 47 pool threads at K5). The pool gate's floor at `task_pool_gate.cpp:608/647` needs the helper in both arms.
5. **Proposed mutants (5b refuted).**
   - The "no prior test" mutant survives natural runs: toy 400 of 400 identical, 0 rejections. It needs a `MHGP9_TESTING` forced-hint hook, e.g. final-chain nodes from a first run.
   - Mutants still to add: no committed bound, untagged hint slot, helper not joined on throw.
6. **Cost claim refuted.** "Commit per facet = hint read + `next[hint]`" is wrong: 1267/1268 and at least two `compressed` loads remain. The ÷1.3–2 is unverifiable, and prior audits bound root search at ≤ 32 % and found no gain from the physical-head ablation.

**Scratch** (not receipts), in `/tmp/claude-1000/-workspaces-E-HGP/71988aca-a49a-4d33-96db-f05468331005/scratchpad/phaseA/verify_p1/`:
- `p1_sim.py` (75f13119…): an interleaved model, an adversarial model and mutants. `sim_2000_s20260926.txt` says `VERDICT ok`.
- `p1_toy.cpp` (b58c570f…): a real helper thread. Outputs in `o2_safe.txt`, `o2_noprior.txt`, `tsan_safe.txt`, `tsan_racy.txt`.
missing: No product-level implementation or CTest was run (the repository is read-only for this lane and the host is saturated). The evidence is abstract models plus a C++ toy transliteration.

No model checker (GenMC/CDSChecker) was run on the relaxed and acquire protocol. The load-buffering and missing-acquire hazards are argued from the C++ memory model and simulated in Python, not observed on hardware (x86 TSO masks them).

The toy's helper hinted only about 0.4 % of facets because of host load, so real-thread timing coverage of the accept path is thin (tens of thousands of acceptances). Deterministic Python adversarial hints carry the branch coverage.
No measurement of P1's benefit or of the helper/committer cache-coherence cost on G4 (Zen 5, cross-CCD).
ARM or other weak-memory targets were not examined.
Helper launch-failure semantics and a failpoint for it are specified but not tested.
The interaction with the `lean_failed` rethrow (1245) was reasoned (hints past the failing block are never consumed) but not exercised in the toy.

verdicts.claim: Per-unit rates of A(K): about 180-190 ns/block (about 700 cycles) and 107-124 ns/facet for K2..K5 on 08/000000; 250-290 ns/node at K5 on all six frames; 300-370 ns/node in K10 runs; K10 order 10 costs 279 ns/block, 154 ns/facet, 360 ns/node.
verdicts.evidence: lots_by_k wraps exactly one order_lots call (src/tower/forest/full_ball_tower.hpp:973-977). R22 probe_0 lots_by_k is [70.7, 51.1, 78.4, 105.7, 147.6]. The sidecar counts (audits/phase_a_20260923/shadow_counts.txt) come from the same input: R22 PACKAGE.json gives scene_00 sha256 0baa4de1..., and the local file hashes the same. K1..5 sums equal probe_0 tower_work (reps 3,621,785, grouped 140,036); K1..10 sums equal probe_2 (17,389,031 and 237,727). Dividing gives 191/189/179/187 ns/block and 124/116/107/109 ns/facet; the medians of 7 repeats (probes 0,12,13,16,18,20,22) give 190/188/179/189 ns/block. ns/node for K2..K5: 00 287-251, 01 275-254, 02 275-247, b00 276-259, b01 276-261, b02 286-260. Probe 14 A(10) = 589.9 ms, i.e. 278.6 ns/block, 154.0 ns/facet, 360 ns/node. K10 ns/node over K2..K10 spans 284-373 across frames.
verdicts.conditions: Per-block and per-facet rates exist only for frame 00. Raw frames give only per-node rates and all-in per-facet rates: sum A / sum reps = 143.5 ns (b00/K5) against 125.2 ns (00/K5), and 165.6 ns against 150.7 ns at K10, so raw is 10-15 % dearer per facet. '700 cycles' needs a core clock the receipt does not record: the TSC runs at 2.7 GHz (lscpu BogoMIPS 5399.99), so 185 ns is 500 TSC ticks. Hop counts come from the ec6d1b74 sidecar; they carry over only because order_root and its call order are unchanged (inference).

verdicts.claim: Fixed per-order costs (anchors.assign, lean zero-fill plus up to 48 thread creations, O(N) live scan) total a few ms, about 3-5 % of A(K) at K5 order 5 and K10 order 10.
verdicts.evidence: No receipt splits order_lots, so this is unmeasured. Least-squares fits over K2..K5 (medians of 7 repeats; scratch verify_cost/fit.py, fit2.py) put the intercept at -0.05 ms with M, 7.4 ms with F and 7.0 ms with N (rms 2-2.6 ms, about the repeat noise). So the fixed part is anywhere from 0 to 7 ms, i.e. 0-5 % of A(5); the data cannot say more. Code-based estimate: anchors.assign writes 4 B per ball for every order (1355), i.e. 5.2 / 11.3 / 22 MB at 00/K5, raw K5 and 00/K10. The lean arrays (7 B per block) are zero-filled on the runner thread alone (1183-1185). Up to 48 fresh threads are created (1192, pool.hpp:328-362), and the parallel count pass reads the catalogue while phase 0 is running. Then the live scan (1402-1404). The cost of one page fault is bounded by process sys time / minor faults: 1.08 s / 501,406 = 2.15 us (probe_0), 1.83 us (probe_24), 2.28 us (probe_26). With 0.5-2.2 us per fault the fixed part comes to 6-16 ms at 00 order 5 (4-11 %), 10-30 ms at raw order 5 (3-9 %) and 13-39 ms at 00 K10 order 10 (2-7 %).
verdicts.conditions: Roughly true for the top order only, and 3-5 % sits at the low end of the code-based range. It does not hold for low orders: the BallId-indexed anchors fill is the same size for every order, so it weighs 10-25 % of A(2) = 51 ms. Order 2 takes 63.4 ms in K10 runs against 50.8 ms in K5 runs (+12.6 ms), and 16.8 MB more anchors per order is one candidate cause.

verdicts.claim: Therefore the per-block loop is at least 90 % of A(K), so the loop is where to cut.
verdicts.evidence: For top orders, 90-96 % is plausible given the fixed-cost estimate above, but it is not measured. reserve_lean (1224-1235) reserves virtual memory only. The first writes, and so the page faults, land inside the loop through push_back and insert (1166-1169, 1297-1298, 1342-1345; full_coverage_certificate.hpp:182-189). d.level.reserve(M+1) at 48 B is 36.2 MiB at 00 order 5 and about 80 MiB at raw order 5 (estimated M5 of about 1.74M = 1.37 x N5). Both exceed glibc's 32 MiB maximum mmap threshold, so each is a fresh mmap, and first touch inside the loop is guaranteed: about 6.8k faults at 00 order 5 and about 15k at raw order 5 for this one array.
verdicts.conditions: 'Loop >= 90 %' must not be read as 'memory latency >= 90 %'. The loop carries a per-byte kernel cost for first-touch faults, estimated at 0-25 % of A(5).

verdicts.claim: About 13.6 random cache-line touches per block (catalogue about 1.7, level_run 2.7, anchors 2.7, compressed 4.7, next 1.7). The dependent chain per facet is anchors -> compressed x2.7 -> next, about 4.7 loads, which gives about 8 L3-latency loads per block, about 400 cycles. The random working set is 19.7 MB at K5 order 5 and 70.3 MB at K10 order 10.
verdicts.evidence: The working-set arithmetic is right: 5.23+5.23+4.61+4.61 MB and 22.05+22.05+13.11+13.11 MB. Toy /tmp/claude-1000/-workspaces-E-HGP/71988aca-a49a-4d33-96db-f05468331005/scratchpad/phaseA/verify_cost/layout.cpp, compiled against src/tower/forest/ball_data.hpp:24-33, gives sizeof(BallData) = 224, level at offset 80 (48 B) and n_shell at offset 130. A catalogue-sized std::vector<BallData> (SealedCatalogue, full_ball_tower.hpp:216-218) comes from glibc mmap with base = 16 mod 64. For half the records the level sits inside the n_shell line, so the level costs exactly 0.5 extra line per record, and the catalogue costs about 1 + 0.5 x batches/M <= 1.37 lines per block, not 1.73. order_root loads compressed at x0..x_h (1151-1152), i.e. hops+1 = 3.74 loads per facet, or 6.4 per block rather than 4.7. x0 is prefetched 8 facets ahead (1261-1265) and anchors 24 ahead (1257-1260). The unprefetched random touches are therefore about 1.37 + 2.71 + 4.7 + 1.71 = 10.5 per block. The critical-path depth is h+2 = 4.74 loads with no prefetch, and about h+1 when the prefetch arrives in time.
verdicts.conditions: These are touches, not misses. Roots are recent nodes at the tail of compressed and next, and may stay hot. '8 L3 loads = 400 cycles' and '700 cycles/block' are projections. level_run is one read-only array shared by all runners, so the relevant L3 pressure is the aggregate, not the per-order figure: about 56 MB at 00/K5 and about 124 MB at b00/K5 when all runners overlap, against 96 MB of L3 over 3 CCDs.

verdicts.claim: 8.1 % of blocks sit in grouped lots at K5 and 1.7 % at K10; lots average 1.05 / 1.01 blocks; 752k lots at K5; the largest lot is 17 / 8 blocks.
verdicts.evidence: shadow_counts.txt: order 5 dsu_slots / blocks = 64,286 / 789,886 = 8.14 %; order 10 36,355 / 2,117,675 = 1.72 %; lots 751,901 give 1.0505 blocks per lot; max_lot is 17 and 8.
verdicts.conditions: True for the top order only. Over all orders of a K5 build the share is 416,138 / 2,164,763 = 19.2 %: K1 61.0 %, K2 45.1 %, K3 22.3 %, K4 13.0 %. After an A/2 cut, K3 and K4 bind the window too (b00 finishes: K5 243.2, K4 240.0, K3 236.8 ms), so their 13-22 % matters for L5. The rejection of P0 stands.

verdicts.claim: Phase A's DSU is order_root path compression on the u64 `compressed` array, not the ranked union-find, which only phase C and the sequential path use.
verdicts.evidence: OrderState::compressed is a std::vector<u64> (757-762) and History::next is a std::vector<u64> (366). order_root does a two-pass full compression (1149-1158) with two requires. The union is order_new_node, which links every parent to the new node (1166-1167): union by time, with no rank. The ranked MonotoneHistoryOf (395-472) is instantiated only at 1560 (phase C) and, through MonotoneHistory, at 643 (the sequential path's lower cursor). anchors is already u32 (759).
verdicts.conditions: Nuance: the sequential path's own-order DSU uses the same path-compression scheme (2054-2056, 2940-2941).

verdicts.claim: R22 helper_threads (409 at K5, 889 at K10) are runners creating threads: up to 48 per order at K>=2 (25 at K1). L1 removes them.
verdicts.evidence: helper_threads is the delta of spawned_threads (590-597). Only run_threads spawns increment it (pool.hpp:328-362, increment at 355); runner threads (946) and phase-B helper std::threads (989) are not counted. Phase-A prepare_lean (1192) uses min(48, ceil(M/4096)) threads: K1 ceil(101,138/4096) = 25, K2..K5 48 each, so 217 at K5 and 457 at K10. Phase-B order_populations (1531, parallel_ranges on the helper) uses 48 per order for K>=2; K1 has no fresh balls, so 192 and 432. 217+192 = 409, 457+432 = 889, frame 01: 22+384 = 406, raw K5: 48+384 = 432.
verdicts.conditions: Only 53 % (K5) and 51 % (K10) come from phase-A runners. L1, for K>=2, removes 192 of 409 and 432 of 889. The phase-B half needs L8.

verdicts.claim: Window projections: dividing all A(K) by 2 or 4 takes 00/K5 from 186 to 116 / 97 ms and b02/K5 from 432 to 250 / 196 ms; at K10, 893 -> 782 / 756, and 391 only with phase 0 / 2 as well.
verdicts.evidence: Recomputed from static_by_k and lots_by_k (scratch verify_cost/window.py). 00/K5: 185.6 -> 115.9 / 96.7. b02: 431.6 -> 250.1 / 196.5. b00: 414.5 -> 243 / 192. 00/K10 (probe 14): 893.0 -> 782 / 756, and 391 with A/4 plus phase 0 / 2. b00/K10: 1647.7 -> 1366 / 1296 / 683. The model matches the measured lots+static to within 0.4 ms, but that match is nearly tautological, because lots_ms is defined as the window minus static (1054). Phase-A code is byte-identical from R18 to R22: I compared order_root, order_new_node, order_prepare_lean, reserve_lean, order_block_lean, order_lot and order_lots at 446b45f7, e9f0a104, 48791e72, d054c1c5 and 43c5ad25. At K5, A(5) is 148 ms in R20 with 82 % phase-0 overlap and 148-150 ms in R22 with 31 %.
verdicts.conditions: The projections assume A(K) does not change when overlap or concurrency changes. That holds within about +-10 % at K5, but not at K10: in the same R21 session, the upper orders run 25-35 % slower with the persistent pool plus hashing (A(10) 423-437 ms against 580-600 ms). At raw K5, A(5) alone binds until every A is cut by about 50 %; it leads K4 by 53 / 37 / 50 ms (b00 / b01 / b02), so a constant cut of c ms per order gains about c.

verdicts.claim: (Summary) A(K) is flat at about 185 ns/block and is bound by memory latency.
verdicts.evidence: This is stated as fact but never established. For it: the per-block rate at K5 does not react to phase-0 overlap (R20 vs R22; R21 arms with the pool and hashing off), which argues against a core-throughput or SMT limit, and larger footprints cost more per facet (raw +10-15 %; order 2 in K10 runs +25 %). Against it: there are no counters and no ablation of the lean loop. The only ablation, physical heads (audits/phase_a_20260923/timed_summary.json), ran on the non-lean ec6d1b74 loop on a contended local host at 971-1149 ns/block, 5-6x the G4 rate, so it says nothing about the current loop. Two alternatives fit the same data equally well. One is first-touch faults: at most 2.2 us each, with at least 6.8k guaranteed at 00 order 5 from the mmap'd level array. The other is branch mispredictions on exits that depend on loaded data (1152-1153, 1247, 1380), which also limit memory-level parallelism.
verdicts.conditions: It is a hypothesis to test with the measurements listed in the summary.

verdicts.claim: Model attribution: page faults 5-13 % of A(K); grouped-lot allocations 5-15 % at K1-K3 and 3-6 % at K5.
verdicts.evidence: The spec labels both as projections. Faults: about 18.6k pages at 00 order 5 (76 MB, which I re-derive at 76.2 MB as an upper bound) times at most 2.2 us gives 0-25 % of A(5) = 148 ms, depending on how many pages are fresh. The mmap'd d.level reservation alone guarantees at least 6.8k fresh pages, which is at least 5 % if a fault costs at least 1 us. Raw order 5 has an estimated 41k pages. Grouped lots: two-regressor fits over K2..K5 give -5 to +464 ns per grouped lot depending on the companion regressor (verify_cost/fit2.py), i.e. 0-8 % at order 5 and 0-30 % at K2, which the data cannot resolve. A code-based count of (7+3 groups) malloc/free pairs plus the owners sort (1306-1321) gives about 0.2-0.5 us per grouped lot, 3-9 % at order 5.
verdicts.conditions: Both need per-thread ru_minflt/ru_stime and the fine rdtsc split of the grouped path.

verdicts.claim: A(1) is inflated by the sequential K1 loop and by running inside phase 0: 43-59 ms in R17-R20, 69-82 ms in R21-R22 at K5.
verdicts.evidence: In the same R21 session, probes 18 and 20 (tower_pipelined_tail=0, tower_hash_grouping=0, tower_persistent_pool=0) give A(1) = 52 / 60 ms against 69-82 ms with those levers on, while A(2..5) stays the same in both arms. Phase-A code is identical from R18 to R22. Even without contention A(1) is about 515-590 ns/block, because of the sequential K1 loop (1210-1218) and 61 % of blocks in grouped lots.
verdicts.conditions: R17's 43 ms predates E3, so it is different code. At K10, A(1) is bimodal (68-137 ms). It does not bind any window.

verdicts.claim: The same order 2 costs 287 ns/node in the K5 run and 356 in the K10 run, so BallId-indexed O(balls) structures and contention cost measurably.
verdicts.evidence: Medians are 285 and 356 ns/node (50.8 and 63.4 ms). Several causes are mixed together: the anchors fill is 4.2x larger (5.2 -> 22 MB), a fixed cost of about 3-13 ms; level_run is 4.2x larger; A(2) in K10 runs alongside about 8 other runners instead of 3; and the phase-0 variant differs.
verdicts.conditions: The direction holds, but the attribution to any one of these causes cannot be separated from the receipts.

verdicts.claim: Suggested order: measure, then L1+L2+L5+L11+L10, then L4+L3, then L6, then P1, then P2.
verdicts.evidence: The receipts and the code support measuring first and doing the zero-risk items before P1. Three amendments. (1) L1's counts alone leave the level copy of published lots (1297/1342) as a full DRAM miss of about 1.1 lines per block, so L2 needs (a) or (b) to remove the catalogue traffic. (2) L6 should move up behind a per-thread minflt measurement, with a zero-risk variant: runners idle until ready[K] (947-956), about 72 ms for runner 5 at raw K5, and could do anchors.assign and pre-touch their M-bounded reservations during that wait. (3) A third software-prefetch stage captures part of P1's gain at no risk.
verdicts.conditions: See the ranking in the summary.

summary:
Lens: cost model and priorities, checked against the G4 R22 receipts. GCP was not used. Nothing heavy was run: only one ~40-line layout toy and some Python fits, all under /tmp/claude-1000/-workspaces-E-HGP/71988aca-a49a-4d33-96db-f05468331005/scratchpad/phaseA/verify_cost/ (layout.cpp, fit.py, fit2.py, window.py). Code references are to morsehgp3D_v9/src/tower/forest/full_ball_tower.hpp at f44a8db03 unless another file is named.

**What is measured and what is inferred.**
- **Measured:**
  - A(K) wall per order (lots_by_k covers the whole of order_lots, 973-977).
  - Object counts: the sidecar input is the same file as R22 scene_00 (sha256 0baa4de1), and its sums equal R22 tower_work.
  - Process-wide sys time, minor faults and involuntary switches (vm/probe_N.stderr).
- **Derived from those:**
  - Rates: 00/K5 K2..K5 is 179-191 ns/block and 107-124 ns/facet; K5 is 247-287 ns/node on all six frames; K10 is 284-373 ns/node; raw frames cost 10-15 % more per facet all-in.
  - The window projections, which reproduce exactly.
  - The helper_threads split: 409 = 217 from phase-A prepare_lean + 192 from phase-B order_populations; 889 = 457 + 432.
  - An upper bound on one page fault of 1.8-2.3 us (sys time / minflt).
- **Natural experiment (measured):** phase-A code is byte-identical from R18 to R22. At K5, A(K>=2) does not react to phase-0 overlap or intensity: A(5) is 148 ms at 82 % overlap in R20 and 148-150 ms at 31 % in R22, and A(2), which runs with no overlap, has the same rate. At K10, in the same R21 session, the upper orders run 25-35 % slower with the persistent pool plus hashing. A(1) is sensitive to phase 0 (52/60 ms vs 69-82 ms) but never binds. The process records only about 1.2-1.5k involuntary context switches per K5 run.
- **Inference only:**
  - that A is bound by memory latency (not established);
